# Spec: undo and redo (v1.11)

**v1.10 (2026-10-29), the authored-ranges amendment (D1a, §4a):** a change is never built
from someone else's text. A fresh diff-based change (an edit, a verb, `write`,
`write --base`'s own hunks, a version restore, an outside save, a person's grouped edit) is
widened to the tokens of the **new** text that hold what it inserted or that it joined
(never past a line break); inside them only the changer's own old characters are kept, and
the rest are deleted and inserted afresh as the change's. Undo, redo, revert and a purge's
removal put back or remove exact elements and are left as they are. Undo regions and revert
records follow the widened hunks (the elements); the hunk channel, carets, views and claims
follow the authored ones. Together with U10a this gives the promise hosts pin verbatim (D1a).
§8 gains the case classes (a)–(c) and three mutants (xii)–(xiv).

**v1.12 (2026-10-30), grids only; text undo is unchanged (S13):** a text's re-paired rows aren't
merged by cell by a reversal. Pairing a text's lines with keys is a guess about identity, so with a
later edit on such a row an undo or redo **conflicts** (`rewritten_row`), and a revert rewrites the
row whole, with the note. A reversal that changes a marked row marks it at its own version. §8 gains
class `row_rewritten_like_another` and mutants (xxix), (xxx), appended so no number shifts.

**v1.14 (2026-10-30), grids only:** S11 takes precedence over S13 in undo, redo and revert. An op
on a re-paired row the doc has dropped is `dropped` (never `rewritten_row`), and a revert never
rewrites such a row whole (a `dropped` conflict, skipped under `--partial`). The oracle's grid
model follows; the kit's mutants (xxxv) and (xxxvi) plant the old orders.

**v1.11 (2026-10-29; v1.10 on the C1 line, renumbered at the merge with kit v0.9.7, whose D1a is v1.10; reviewed by K2 Engine, m_69RTlaV9BH: "the structure is sound"):**
**structured kinds**
(MovableList, Map, and tables composed of them), §6a, from the CSV seam design §7.3 and
the approved amendment G1-5 (K-HIST-16). v1.9's text rules are **unchanged**. A region is
an element facet; a conflict is judged by **write identity**, never by value; a restored
write counts as the write it restores (U23 for elements); the caller's **own later writes
count as anyone's** (S3: the conservative rule, which is v1.9's for text); a header switch
is one region (S7); a region whose live facet already equals what the undo would write is
`already`, applied by nobody and overwriting nothing (S3a, O4's principle); a dropped element
can't be undone and `drop-deleted` is on no stack (S4, S11); a version restore never reuses a
dropped key (S12, not an undo rule). A holder with no identity is a Yrs-only case (S2).
§6's rows for List, MovableList, Map and Table are superseded by §6a. §8 gains the
structured case classes and mutants (xv)–(xxviii). *Addendum (2026-10-29):* restore → delete
also needs every covering undel that isn't own in the batch's causal past (S4, G1-8 §3); mutant
(xxvii), model-and-native only. *Agreed (K2 Engine, m_mnjjaNtJfm):* move → move back anchors on the
old left neighbour in place order, deleted or not (S4); mutant (xxviii).
**Model revision (2026-10-29), no rule change:** the Quint model (`spec/quint/undo.qnt`) now
builds a purge's removal as **canonical hunks** (copies that touch are one hunk), as D2, U8
and U9 already say and as the oracle and the kit do; it had read them as one hunk per copy.
No rule, outcome or kit behaviour changes; the model check's exact counts at bounds with a
revert and a purge change with it (`docs/MODEL-CHECK.md`, `docs/evidence/g1-undo.md`).

**v1.9 (2026-10-28):** wording and checks, no change to what the kit does (from the model
check's fidelity review of v1.8). **O4a** says where the live root is looked for: in the
root's live text **as the step merges it** (after the earlier steps of the request), window
included. **U10a** is read over the regions a step **applies**: a region skipped under
`--partial` lends its roots to no other region (v1.8 took every region of the batch, which
only I1 made the same). **I1** is checked **after every step** of an undo or redo: the kit
commits each step as its own change (its own change ID and record, all of a request's steps
in one durable append, U13). §8 gains mutant (xi) `no-o4a` (O4 on roots, no O4a; fails I1).

**v1.8 (2026-10-28):** **provenance** for restored text (U23). An element an undo, redo or
revert puts back records the **root** it restores (path-compressed, never a chain); it is
still a new element (U18a). The rules follow the root: a window's elements are read **by
root** (U8), so text someone else removed and put back is the base's again; U10a becomes
"removes only elements whose root the reversed change inserted"; revert targets the live
elements whose root its change inserted (U22). Two v1.7 outcomes go back to the expected
ones: **(a)** a revert of a change undone and redone applies; **(b)** after b edits inside
a's region and undoes it, a's undo applies. **O4** is judged on (position, root), not on
text; **O4a** refuses to put back a root that is live; invariant **I1**: at most one live
element per root. Blame reports the **root's** change and author plus the restoring change
(U18a). Only the kit stamps provenance (`sec.client_provenance_refused`). §8 gains the case
class "concurrent restores of one root" and mutant (x) `provenance-ignored-in-O4`.

**v1.7 (2026-10-28):** undo, redo and revert merge **exact hunk sets**, never re-diffed
strings (finding F3). U10 and the merge inputs are restated on hunk sets: **ours** is the
inverse of the batch's own recorded hunks, **theirs** the foreign hunks from the
applied-hunk stream that touched the region's carried window, composed in the region's base
coordinates. A region carries its theirs (U8, U6). **U10a** makes `hist.undo_own_only`
normative: undo, redo and revert never remove an element they didn't write. **U12** is
restated on hunk sets; the old re-diff equivalence is an informative note (finding F4).
U17's redo region, U22's revert record and U22a carry the same sets. `diff::hunks` is used
only where there is no history: `restore` and `write --base`. §8 gains the restart action
in the model check, two mutants ((viii) re-diff, (ix) single restart taint) and the case
class "exact sides differ from a re-diff".

**v1.6 (2026-10-28):** U22a's restart sentence dropped: a carry persisted when the revert
window moves keeps **each edge's** taint, so a host restart changes no revert's outcome
(restart transparency). v1.5 let a reloaded carry taint both edges of a region tainted at
one, so the same record and the same later edits could give a different conflict set after
a restart. §8 gains the restart-transparency property and its trace class.

**v1.5 (2026-10-28):** U10 clarified (a clean region applies the merge's own hunks, never a
re-diff of the window); U22a added (revert's carried taint, exactly, with its superset
property); U19's notice settled (said once, withdrawn by the holder's next batch). The
trace test (§8) gains a repeated-text case class.

The kit's definition of undo, redo and revert. Its oracle of record is `spec_undo::model`
(`crates/spec-undo`); the kit's implementation is `crates/base/src/session/undo.rs`. Rule ids
(U\*, O\*, D\*) are stable; the oracle's doc comments and the trace test cite them.

One definition of undo, redo and revert for **every engine** behind the kit, written over
**plain values**: text strings and the hunks that changed them. **Undo is implemented once, in
the kit** (`session/undo.rs`) and runs unchanged over every engine. The engine's only part is
to report, for **every change it applies** (agent edits, restores, undo/redo/revert
applications and, later, concurrent client batches integrated by CRDT merge), the hunk
sequence in **host apply order at element-identity positions**: each inserted or deleted
element reported at its actual index, so that replaying the hunks over the previous text gives
the new text byte for byte *and* repeated text can't hide a wrong position. It also delivers
atomic multi-root apply, group IDs, stable change IDs and purge notices. No undo logic lives
in the engine. The kit owns this spec; a change to it is reviewed by the engine's owners.

**What "one semantics on every engine" means.** Undo is one function of the applied-hunk
stream. Engines agree wherever their merges agree, and differ exactly where the Fugue paper's
Def. 4 says YATA (Yrs) is wrong: YATA and FugueMax order concurrent same-spot inserts
differently by design, so under concurrency their texts, and therefore their undo outcomes,
can differ there. The test requires **equality on serialised traces** and, under concurrency,
**equality wherever the merged texts agree** (the generator is biased so that ≥ 90% of
concurrency traces agree), with every other difference classified by a Def. 4 checker.
Demanding exact equality would demand YATA's interleaving.

Notation: a *hunk* is `(start, end, insert)` on UTF-8 byte offsets (`text/diff.rs`).
`merge3(base, ours, theirs)` is the kit's three-way merge (`text/merge.rs`);
`merge3_window(base, ours, theirs, at_end)` is the same merge on a slice of a doc, where
`at_end` says whether the slice ends at the doc's end (§4).

**Scope: which paths use this spec.** Only **`undo`, `redo`, `revert` and `write --base`** go
through `merge3` and this spec. **An editor client's keystroke stream stays a CRDT branch
merge**: concurrent typing never conflicts, and both end-of-text appends land in the engine's
order.

**The diff is deterministic** (D1–D3, §4a): `merge3` is built on `diff::hunks`, so the spec
pins that function.

## 1. Batches and stacks

| # | Rule |
|---|---|
| U1 | A **batch** is one change by one participant: one `edit` / `edit_with` / `write --base` / `replace_text` / `revert` call, one verb (CLI), one `restore`, or one person **undo group** (U3). A batch may touch several roots; it is undone and redone as one unit. Every batch has a **stable change ID** that outlives the session. |
| U2 | Every batch is recorded on the **undo stack of its pid** (not its connection): one pid's tabs, devices and terminal share one stack. *(Open question: whether a per-surface stack is better; this spec changes if it is.)* An assistant agent has one stack for all the people it acts for; its plain `undo` undoes its newest batch whoever it was for, and `undo --for <person>` restricts it to batches made on that person's behalf. |
| U3 | **Person grouping (editor clients).** The **client proposes** groups: consecutive local edits from one connection form one group until any of (a) **500 ms** with no edit; (b) a non-contiguous edit; (c) a **word boundary** (a space, tab or punctuation typed after a word character); (d) a newline; (e) a command that isn't typing (paste, cut, format, find-replace, drag); (f) an undo or redo. **(g)** The **host-side kit splits** a group where another participant's change lands inside or touching the group's span **in host apply order** (the client can't know this; its keystrokes may integrate after foreign ops it hasn't seen). The engine records client group IDs and timestamps and never groups on its own. Agents never group: one verb = one batch. *Kit (v0.9.7, K4):* the client's token is `EditOptions::group`; the kit applies (a)–(g) on what the host sees, with (a)'s idle from `Config::undo_group_idle_ms` (default **1 s**, not yet reconciled with (a)'s 500 ms) on the host clock; `docs/SESSIONS.md`, "Person grouping". |
| U4 | **Not undoable by anyone:** `import` and `external` changes (no participant stack). They are reversed with `restore --version` (a version is cut before every external edit). A raw-tool write attributed to a merely *probable* agent is **not** put on that agent's stack. `revert` (U22) can reverse them where the rights allow. |
| U5 | `restore` and `revert` are the caller's batches and are undoable by them. Undo and redo are themselves recorded as the undo/redo stacks, not as new undoable batches: undoing an undo is `redo`. |
| U6 | **Bounds.** Per pid per doc: at most **100 batches** and **4 MiB** of retained region text; the oldest batches are dropped first. Stacks live in the session: they **survive leave and rejoin**, and are **lost on session unload and host restart** (every engine alike). `revert` (U22) doesn't depend on them. |
| U7 | Any new batch by a pid **clears that pid's redo stack**. Other participants' edits don't. |

## 2. What undo computes (text)

For a batch B on root r with text `S_before` before it and `S_after` after it, and the live
text `L` now:

| # | Rule |
|---|---|
| U8 | **Regions are hunks.** Each **canonical hunk** of B on r, as the applied stream reports it (D2: sorted, non-overlapping, coalesced when touching), is **one region** `[s, e)` with `R_before = S_before[s..e_before]` and `R_after = S_after[s..e]`. A batch has as many regions as hunks; a `sed -i` touching lines 3 and 300 is two regions. Each region's bounds are carried through **every later change to r, by anyone**, like a caret: a later hunk entirely before the region shifts it; an insertion **exactly at the region's start or end is pulled inside it**; a later hunk entirely after leaves it alone. **Shared edges within one step:** canonical hunks don't touch when recorded, but later deletes by others can make two regions of the same step touch; a foreign insertion exactly at their shared edge is pulled into the **left** region only, never both. **Theirs** (v1.7): each region also carries the foreign hunks that touched its window since the batch, composed into one canonical hunk set (D2's form) in the coordinates of `R_after`: a later hunk is **inside** the window when it lies within the carried bounds (a pure insertion exactly at an edge included: pulled in); its elements replace the window's elements it covers. Which base elements are gone and which foreign elements stand where is read off by element identity, never by diffing the window's text. At a shared edge the right region drops, from the front of its theirs, the foreign elements the left one took. A tainted region (U9) keeps no theirs. Theirs counts toward U6's budget. **By root** (v1.8): the window's elements are matched to the base's by **provenance root** (U23), not by element: scanning the live window left to right, an element whose root is base element *i*'s root **counts as base element *i*** when *i* is greater than the last base index counted; every other element is foreign. So a base element someone removed and then put back (an undo, redo or revert of theirs) is the base's again, and theirs is read off the counted base elements exactly as above. Where no restoration is involved this is v1.7's element identity. |
| U9 | **Taint.** If any later hunk deletes across a region edge (it starts strictly before an edge and ends strictly after it), the region is **tainted**. A tainted region always conflicts (U11). |
| U10 | **Undo of one region** (v1.7) = the merge of two **exact hunk sets** on `R_after` (§4's pair rules O1–O5 and placement): **ours** = the inverse of the batch's own recorded hunk for the region, as made (`[0, |R_after|) → R_before`), and **theirs** = the region's carried foreign hunks (U8), whose application to `R_after` is the live window `L[s'..e']`. Before v1.7 this read `merge3_window(base = R_after, ours = R_before, theirs = L[s'..e'], at_end)`, with both sides found by `diff::hunks`; in repeated text that diff can't tell a foreign element from the region's own (F3: seed `ab`, p1 replaces `a` with `b`, p2 inserts `b` at 0, and p1's undo deleted p2's `b`). The window and its flag: where `[s', e')` are the carried bounds and **`at_end` is true only if `e'` equals the live doc's length and the whole doc was non-empty in the merge's base**. "Non-empty" is judged on the merge's base, the whole doc as it stood when the undone change was made, not on the live doc: `at_end = e' == live.len() && !merge_base_doc_was_empty`. Case: B deletes the whole doc, then someone appends; undoing B's delete is judged with base = "" and is a conflict, consistently with U12's whole-text merge3; the region's own base `R_after` may be empty, e.g. after B deleted the last line, and that must not block O5. **Within one step, regions apply back to front** (highest `s'` first), each application carrying the bounds of the regions not yet applied. So the end-of-text rule (O5) applies only at the doc's real end, never at the end of a region in mid-text. A clean merge gives the inverse hunks (offset by `s'`); otherwise the region conflicts. **The step applies exactly those hunks** (v1.5): the merge's own, ours' changes placed in theirs' coordinates, **never a fresh diff of the window**. Hunks name elements (element identity): in repeated text a diff of the window can name another participant's identical characters, giving the same text with the wrong elements, so that participant's own undo later finds nothing to remove. The same holds for redo and revert, and for `write --base`'s clean merge. |
| U10a | **Own elements only** (v1.7; restated on roots in v1.8, `hist.undo_own_only`, normative): an undo, redo or revert removes only live elements whose **root** (U23) is one that **the change it reverses inserted**: an undo of batch B, the roots of B's inserted elements; a redo, the roots the undo step put back; a revert of change C, the roots of C's inserted elements. **Read over the regions the step applies** (v1.9): the roots the reversed change inserted *in those regions*; a region skipped under `--partial` lends its roots to no other (by I1 the two readings agree; this one does not lean on it). For an undo of an edit that is the undoer's own text, so **undo never removes text whose origin is someone else's** (F3's safety). With exact sets read by root this is a consequence of U8 and U10 (ours removes only base elements; an element counts as a base element only by its root), and the conformance suite, the oracle, the model check and the trace test each **fail** on a violation. *v1.7's consequence with U18a is withdrawn:* when someone edits inside your region and then undoes their edit, the text they put back has your roots, so **your undo applies** (regression (b)); a change undone and redone has its roots live again, so **its revert applies** (regression (a)). *(For an undo of an edit, "the removed text's root author is the undoer"; for a redo, or an undo of a revert, the removed roots are the ones the reversed step put back, which may be another author's.)* |
| U11 | **Conflict region (what is reported).** For each conflicting region: `{root, live byte range [s', e'), live lines (first, last) 1-based, kind: overlap / taint}`. One entry per conflicting region (= hunk), never sub-ranges of a hunk. Every engine reports exactly this wherever their merged texts agree. |
| U12 | **Equivalence** (v1.7, on hunk sets). Outside the taint case, U10 equals the whole-text merge of the **same exact sets** placed in the doc (ours and theirs offset by `s'`, the rest of the doc as base), because changes outside a region can't overlap it (§4), and because U10 passes `at_end` exactly when the region ends at the doc's end **and the whole doc's base was non-empty**, which is exactly when whole-text O5 can fire. *Informative (F4):* the pre-v1.7 statement "U10 equals whole-text `merge3` of the same inverse on L" compared **re-diffed** sides and fails in repeated text (seed `ab`; p1 inserts `a` at 0; p2 replaces it with `b`: the window form conflicts by identity, a whole-text diff deletes the seed's `a` instead and is clean); it holds wherever a diff of the strings gives the exact sets. **Worked case:** B deletes the last line `x\n` of `a\nx\n`; someone appends `y\n`; undo calls `merge3_window("", "x\n", "y\n", at_end = true)` (the doc's base `a\n` is non-empty) and lands `a\ny\nx\n`, theirs first, exactly as whole-text merge3 does. The region form is the definition; it costs memory in proportion to the edit, not the doc. |

## 3. Modes

| # | Rule |
|---|---|
| U13 | **`undo [--steps N]`** (default N = 1) is **all-or-nothing**. Plan the newest N batches newest-first against L, applying each planned step to a scratch copy and carrying the remaining regions through it (U8). If **any** region of any step conflicts, apply **nothing**, report every conflicting region of the **first** conflicting step, and exit 1 (`undo_conflict`). Otherwise apply all N steps as **one log append**, recorded as N redo entries. |
| U14 | **`undo --partial [--steps N]`** applies, per step, every region that merges cleanly and skips and reports every region that conflicts; exit 0 if nothing was skipped, 1 if anything was. A step with at least one applied region is consumed (moved to redo with its skipped regions marked). **A step whose every region conflicts is not consumed:** it stays on top of the stack, nothing is applied, and the reply says so; with N > 1 planning stops there. **Escape:** `undo --drop` removes the blocked top step without applying it (reported; it does not go to redo); in an editor, a second Ctrl+Z on the same blocked step offers "skip this change", which is `--drop`. |
| U15 | **Identical reports.** For the same batch and the same L, the conflicting regions reported by `undo` (U13) and skipped by `undo --partial` (U14) are the same set. With N > 1 this holds for the **first** conflicting step. |
| U16 | **A person's Ctrl+Z in an editor is `undo --partial` with N = 1**, subject to U21. Ctrl+Shift+Z is `redo` with N = 1. |
| U17 | **`redo [--steps N]`** reapplies, newest-undone first, **exactly the regions that the undo applied** (skipped regions are not redone). Redo of a region (v1.7) merges exact sets on **`R_before'`, the region's live text just after the undo applied it**: ours = **the inverse of the hunks the undo applied there** (giving `R_after'`, its text just before), theirs = the foreign hunks since (U8). So redo inverts exactly what the undo did, element for element. Redo is all-or-nothing by default and has `--partial` with the rules of U13–U15. Because U14 never consumes an all-conflicting step, a redo entry always has at least one region. **Ordering note:** undoing a delete of the last line after someone else appended at the doc's end re-inserts the line **after** their append (O5: theirs first), **cleanly** (O5's non-empty base is the whole doc's, not the region's). |
| U18 | Nothing to undo or redo: exit 0 with `nothing to undo`. After a host restart the reply says the history was lost with the session (U6) and points at `revert`. |
| U18a | **Blame after undo** (v1.8): undo, redo and revert insert **new** elements (new IDs, the undoer's batch), so anchors and cursors that pointed into the removed text don't come back, on every engine. Each restored element records its provenance root (U23), and **blame reports the root**: a live character maps to its **provenance-root insert** (the change that first inserted the element it restores, and that change's author), plus the **restoring event** (the undo, redo or revert change that put it back, and its author) as a second field. A line goes to its character with the greatest root change id. `text.blame_char` and `hist.blame_grain` say the same. |
| U23 | **Provenance** (v1.8). Every element has a **provenance root**. An element inserted by an edit, `write --base`, `replace_text`, `restore`, an import or an external change is **its own root**. An element an undo, redo or revert inserts puts back an element *d* that the reversed change removed (every element ours inserts does: ours inserts only what the change removed, U10, U17), and records **`restores_root = root(d)`**, computed when it is made, so roots are **never chains**. It is a new element (new ID, the undoer's batch): no tombstone comes back, and the rules read the root, not the element: U8 (by root), U10a, U22, O4, O4a, I1 and blame (U18a). **Only the kit stamps provenance**, in its own undo, redo and revert; it is never taken from a client update, on any path (`sec.client_provenance_refused`). It survives restart and reload: the kit persists each restored element's root and each revert record's inserted and deleted roots (store format 5, an in-place upgrade from 4 in which every existing element is its own root). Provenance holds element IDs only, never content (a purge has nothing more to redact; U19 still clears the stacks). |
| U21 | **Ctrl+Z with unacked or offline edits.** Ctrl+Z targets **acked** batches only. An unsent local batch is cancelled on the client before anything is sent; a sent but unacked one is waited for. The undo request carries the client's last group ID, and the host applies it only after integrating that client's ops up to it. **Offline**, Ctrl+Z only drops the client's own unacked local ops; past them it is disabled with a hint until reconnect. **Re-based ops:** **the host is the only re-base owner**: a client never re-bases; the host re-bases a dropped client's ops against the recorded view and the client adopts the typed `rebased{epoch,…}` frame. Re-based ops **keep their client group IDs**, and an undo request waiting on a group that is being re-based waits for the host's `rebased` frame. |
| U22 | **`revert <change>`.** Reverses **one named change** (its stable change ID) using **U8–U11 on its persisted revert record**: the change's hunks, deleted text, author and `on_behalf_of`, and its regions' **carried bounds and taint flag**. **No per-keystroke work over all records:** a record is written once, at the change; its bounds are **relative positions** (Yrs `StickyIndex`; element IDs on an engine that has them) or live in an **offset tree with O(log R) work per apply** (R = records held) with batched persistence; taint is marked **lazily** from an interval index of later deletions and resolved when the record is used. So log compaction of later changes can't strand the carry, and a busy doc's keystroke cost doesn't grow with R (benchmark target: ≤ 20 µs p95 per apply at R = 10^5). Revert works days later and after host restarts, independent of stacks, **inside the revert window**: all pending on-behalf changes, plus changes from the last 30 days or the last 10,000 changes per doc (whichever reaches further), ≤ 64 MiB per doc. Outside it, revert returns **`revert_too_old`**, **exit 8** (never a retry-after, unlike conflicts' exit 1) pointing at `restore --version`. **Pending on-behalf records are capped at 1,000 records or 16 MiB per doc**; past it new on-behalf edits are refused (`held: approvals_backlog`, exit 2) so revertability is never silently lost. A region overlapping a **redacted** span is a conflict of kind **`erased`**. On an engine whose positions derive from element IDs, reach may differ; the trace test compares only inside the shared retention. `revert --partial` follows U14 (except that "not consumed" doesn't apply: a fully conflicting revert applies nothing and exits 1). **Theirs for revert** (v1.7) is the foreign hunks inside each region's carried window since the change, taken from the stored shapes of every later change (positions and lengths, kept for the doc's life; the inserted text is the live window's), so the persisted record needs **no new field and the store format is unchanged**; it costs O(L) in the changes since, at revert time only. **Revert targets roots** (v1.8): the record's region is read by root (U8), so revert of C acts on the live elements whose root C inserted. A change that was **undone and redone** has its roots live again (the redo put them back, U23): **its revert applies** (v1.7 conflicted). The record keeps its inserted and deleted elements' roots (U23, store format 5); a record written before format 5 has none, and is reverted as in v1.7. Allowed for the change's author, its `on_behalf_of` person and the doc's owner; recorded as a new batch of the reverter. While an on-behalf change is `pending`, its revert record is kept whatever the window says. Revert records are purge-reachable (U19). |
| U22a | **Revert's carried taint (v1.5), exactly.** A revert record's region edges are carried each on its own (no shared-edge clamp while carrying; the clamp of U8 applies when the record is used), and each edge has its own taint flag (U9 per edge). When the record is used, its regions are taken in record order (by root, then start); a region whose carried start is at or before the previous region's carried end on the same root **inherits that end's taint**; then the shared-edge clamp (U8) gives the bounds (the right region drops the foreign elements at its front that the left region holds), and U10–U11 apply with each region's theirs over its own carried window. A carry persisted when the revert window moves (records kept as pending on-behalf, older than the move) keeps **each edge's taint**, as the live carry does (v1.6), so **revert is restart-transparent**: the same record and the same later edits give the same outcome with or without a host restart at any point. **Properties** (tested): on the same state, revert's conflicting regions are a superset of undo's for the same change, with the same bounds, and every region both apply gives the same text; and a restart at any point changes no revert's outcome. |

## 4. Overlap rules (merge3, shared with `write --base`)

| # | Rule |
|---|---|
| O1 | Two non-empty ranges that intersect conflict. |
| O2 | An insertion strictly inside the other side's non-empty range conflicts. |
| O3 | Touching at a boundary does not conflict: an insertion at the start of the other side's range lands before it; one at its end lands after it. |
| O4 | An identical change on both sides is taken once. **Judged on (position, root)** (v1.8), not on text: two hunks are identical when they have the same range on the base and insert elements with the **same roots in the same order**. A fresh `X` someone typed where an undo would put back `X` is not that `X` (no longer taken once; O5 decides). For `write --base` (no history: both sides are diffs) identical means equal hunks, as before. |
| O4a | **A root is put back at most once** (v1.8). An undo, redo or revert never inserts an element whose root is live: if a hunk of ours that O4 didn't take once would put back an element whose root is live **in the live text as the step merges it** (after the earlier steps of the request; anywhere in it, the region's window included), the region **conflicts** (kind `overlap`). *(v1.9 wording; v1.8 read "live anywhere in that root's text".)* |
| O0 | **The sides** (v1.7). For undo, redo and revert both sides are exact hunk sets (U10); for `write --base` they are the closed texts' whole-line diffs, `diff::whole_line_hunks(closed(base), closed(ours))` and the same for theirs (there is no history to name elements; v0.9.7.1: every hunk covers and writes whole lines, so two changes touching one line always overlap and nothing is merged inside a line; the final "\n" of a clean merge follows the side that wrote the last line, and its applied hunks are the verb edits' diff from the live text to the merged text). Before v0.9.7.1 they were `diff::hunks` (to v0.9.7), whose character trim could pair lines sharing a start one line off. O1–O5 read either the same way. |
| O5 | Two different insertions at the **same point** conflict, **except at the end of the live doc when the whole doc was non-empty before the merge**, where both land: **theirs first, then ours** (theirs is already live). This makes "two agents append to a log" non-conflicting. **Not** at the end of a window that isn't the doc's end (`merge3_window(.., at_end = false)`), and **not** when the **whole doc** was empty before the merge (the doc's base, never a region's): two `write --base` calls on a new, empty doc conflict (CT `merge.empty_base_same_point_conflicts`). merge3 is therefore **symmetric up to the order of two different end-of-text appends** (`clean_merges_are_symmetric_up_to_eof_order`), and O5 never changes a merge that was already clean without it (`eof_rule_only_adds_clean_merges`). |
| O5a | **The end of the text, `write --base` only** (amendment "O5 end-of-text" r3). The texts merge closed (O0), so a line one side wrote after the other left the text open is its own line: the merged text holds one line break there, in the writer's applied change (its undo and revert remove it, and it is in the E-LIVE window as part of that change's hunks). The final line break follows the side that wrote the last line; for a base line both kept, or a line both wrote, the side that changed the base's ending (ours when it did). There is no separate pass. The cases are the trace classes `end_break_a`…`end_break_d`. **Not** in undo, redo or revert (U10's windows): they put back exact elements (U23). |
| O6 | **A refused `write --base`'s regions** (v0.11.1, a clarification of the kit's behaviour, no change): conflicting hunks of the two sides (O1, O2, O5) whose ranges on the base overlap or touch form one region, reported once, with its base range and its lines (in the base, in ours and in theirs) the union of those hunks'. **A region's sides** (v0.11.1, a fix): a side's text of the region is the base range with **every** hunk of that side inside it applied, its clashing ones and any other there (an insertion where two clashes touch clashes with nothing, O3, yet lands inside the region); its lines are where that text stands in that side's whole text (`MPC-E111`'s `your_lines` and `current_lines`). An insertion at the region's start or end is outside it: it lands before or after the region, as O3 places it; an empty region (two insertions at one point) holds that point's insertions only. Before v0.11.1 the kit rendered a side from its clashing hunks alone, leaving such an insertion out of the side's text and lines. |

**Invariant I1** (v1.8): **at most one live element per provenance root**, in every state, on every engine. O4 and O4a keep it when two restorations of one root meet (b deletes a's `X`; b undoes, giving `X1` with root `X`; c deletes `X1`; then c's undo and a's revert of b's delete both want root `X` back: whichever comes second finds it identical, O4, or live, O4a). **Each step of an undo or redo is its own change** (its own change ID and revert record; a request's steps are one durable append, U13), so **I1 holds after every step**, not only after the request (v1.9). It is checked in the kit (a debug assertion as each step's restorations enter the live-root index, and tests), and, after every step, in the oracle, the enumerator and the Quint model.

## 4a. The diff is deterministic

| # | Rule |
|---|---|
| D1 | The edit pipeline is **`align_insertions(diff::hunks(old, new))`** (pure line insertions are anchored at line starts), and every part of it is a **pure function of its inputs**. `diff::hunks(old, new)` is a **pure function of its inputs**: no wall-clock deadlines, no machine-load dependence. The search is bounded by a **counted work budget** (`text/myers.rs`: 2^22 units plus 16 per input byte per call), the same on every machine; past it, the result is a coarser but still correct diff, identically everywhere. *(Root cause recorded: an earlier merge3 identity failure came from wall-clock deadlines.)* |
| D1a | **Authored ranges** (v1.10). A fresh change's **authored ranges** are its hunks as the participant made them: every hunk of the diff for `replace_text`, `write`, `sed`, a restore and an outside save (text the diff leaves equal is not authored), **ours' hunks only** for `write --base`'s merge3 (what merge3 kept from the live text is not), the hunks as sent for an edit. Each is **widened to the tokens of the new text** that hold what it inserted, or that it joined by deleting what separated them, by the pack's tokens (whitespace-delimited words by default, identifier and punctuation tokens for code, the cell for CSV), **never past a line break**; a token the change only shortened, or split with a separator, creates no new content and stays its authors'. Inside a widened range an old element is kept only if its provenance root's author is the changer; every other one is deleted and its text, where still present, inserted afresh as the change's. Outside the widened ranges nothing is touched, and within one's own text character-level reuse is unchanged. The engine, the provenance map, undo regions (U8) and the revert record (U22) take the widened hunks; the hunk channel, carets, views, claims and the change summary take the authored ones (the same text), and the store keeps a widened change's authored hunks beside its record. Undo, redo, revert and a purge's removal give their roots and are not widened. **The promise** (with U10a, at token granularity), the sentence hosts pin verbatim: *"Undo only reverses your own changes and never alters a word someone else wrote: if someone has since changed one of your words, that word is theirs, and your undo leaves it as it is and tells you."* Under character tokens (the model check's single-letter alphabets) D1a is the identity. |
| D2 | **Canonical hunks:** sorted, non-overlapping, never empty, coalesced when touching, on character boundaries. For repeated substrings the **tie-break is the implementation's, pinned by golden tests** (`tie_break_is_pinned`): the common prefix is trimmed first, so `"aa"→"aaa"` inserts at position 2, which keeps an appended duplicate last line an end-of-text append for O5. **`spec_undo::model` calls `diff::hunks`; it doesn't reimplement it**, so the diff is a shared dependency whose correctness is carried by the diff's own tests. Changing the tie-break is a spec change. |
| D3 | `merge3` inherits D1–D2, so undo, redo, revert and `write --base` give the same result on every machine. **Not built yet:** the trace test (§8) should run each trace twice under different CPU load and on aarch64 and x86_64 and require byte-identical outcomes; today it runs each seed once, on x86_64. |

## 5. Erasure

| # | Rule |
|---|---|
| U19 | **A purge clears every undo and redo stack for that doc, and redacts the purged content in revert records.** Holders see `undo history cleared by purge` **once**, on their next undo or redo that finds nothing; a new batch by the holder withdraws it (from then on, plain `nothing to undo`) (v1.5). This is the simplest rule that guarantees no purged content, not even part of a secret typed in two batches, can return through undo; a purge is a rare owner action. Stacks keep **no content hash** of anything. `revert` (U22) still works for every other change: it reads the log, where purged content is redacted, so a revert can never restore it either. |
| U20 | **Participant erasure** keeps stacks keyed by the pseudonymised pid; the erased person's own stack is dropped. |

## 6. Non-text kinds (definition level)

The kit's rule for every kind: **undo restores your own previous state only where nobody has
changed it since. It never overwrites another participant's later change**; that case is a
conflict (`--partial` skips it). This deliberately differs from many apps' register undo
(Stewen & Kleppmann, PaPoC 2024, §2): an agent's undo must not clobber a person. Each element
is a region.

| Kind | A batch records | Undo of one element | Conflict when |
|---|---|---|---|
| Map (per key) | key, value before, value after | set the key back to "before" (or delete it if it was absent) | the key's live value ≠ "after" |
| List | inserted item IDs; deleted items with neighbours; set-item before/after | delete own inserted items still present; re-insert own deleted items next to their surviving left neighbour; set items back | an own inserted item was changed by someone else; a re-insert's left and right neighbours are both gone; a set item ≠ "after" |
| MovableList | the moved item, position before, position after | move it back to "before" | **someone else moved the item since** (its position register was written after this batch), or the item is gone. Index changes from others' inserts or deletes elsewhere are not conflicts |
| Tree | the node, parent and index before and after | move back | **someone else moved the node since**, the old parent is gone, or the move back would create a cycle. Sibling index changes from others' edits are not conflicts |
| Table | per its parts: rows and columns (MovableList), cells (Map) | per part | per part |
| Blob pointer | pointer before and after | set it back | the live pointer ≠ "after" |

The modes (§3), identical reports (U15), redo (U17), revert (U22) and purge (§5) apply
unchanged, with "region" read as "element".

*§6's rows for List, MovableList, Map and Table are superseded by §6a (v1.11): §6's
"live value ≠ after" is a value comparison, which v1.11 replaces by write identity (S3).*

## 6a. Structured kinds (v1.11)

Over **elements by key**, for MovableList and Map roots and the tables composed of them
(rows and columns MovableLists, cells, names, quoting and meta Maps; CSV contract §1.1). A
**write** is one op's write identity (`WriteId` on Yrs, an event ID on native); the kit's
index of who holds each facet (`ELEM_WRITES` on Yrs, `winner()` on native, cross-checked in
the shadow) answers "who holds it now". Everything is by key: no positions are stored or
carried, so nothing is ever diffed (F3 can't happen) and no taint exists.

| # | Rule |
|---|---|
| S1 | **Regions are element facets.** A batch's regions are the `(root, key, facet)` its ops wrote (effect not `none`), read from its **own record** (the ops by key with their writes, values before and after, the live key before each list op, and the facet's previous holder: revert record v3). Facets: a list element's **value**, **position** (its last insert or move) and **existence** (its last insert, delete or restore); a map key's **value**. One op is one region unless S7 groups it. **A step's regions are taken newest op first**, each judged on the doc as the step's earlier regions leave it (an exact inverse: a sort's moves depend on each other); holders are read as they stood before the step, which within one batch changes nothing (every write of a batch is its own). |
| S2 | **The holder, resolved.** A facet's **holder** is the write that holds it now. A write made by an undo, redo or revert that put an earlier write back (a value set back, an element moved back, a delete undone or redone) **records the write it restores** (`restores_write`, U23 for elements, stamped by the kit only), on **every facet** it writes (value, position and existence), and **counts as that write**, path-compressed, never a chain. **The kit's own writes always carry their batch's identity** in the holder index, map deletes and restores included. Only a write **merged in from elsewhere** whose writer the engine doesn't report has **no identity**, and it resolves to nothing. **No identity is Yrs-only:** on native every write (set, delete, undel, move) is an event, so a holder always resolves and KC7 can't arise; the case class that expects a conflict from a holder with no identity is a **pinned Yrs deviation** (the conservative direction), not a rule native must reproduce. *Engine half (K2 Engine's next addendum):* E-HIST-17 widens `restores_write` to the position and existence facets; `winner(elem, existence)` is defined under delete-wins (hidden: the highest `(lamport, agent)` delete not covered by an undel; live: the latest covering undel, else the insert). |
| S3 | **Own and conflict.** A region is **own** when its holder, **resolved (S2), is the batch's own write for that facet, resolved**: a write that restores another counts as it on both sides (a redo reverses its undo's restoring writes; two writes restoring one write are that write). Undo of a region **conflicts when it isn't**: somebody, **the caller included**, wrote that facet since and that write still holds it, or the holder has no identity (KC7; Yrs only, S2). *Why the caller's own later writes count as anyone's (question 1):* (a) it is v1.9's rule for text: a region's theirs is every later hunk, the undoer's own included; (b) in the normal LIFO order the caller's later batch is undone **first**, and its undo's writes restore this batch's writes (S2), so this batch's undo then finds its regions own and applies: LIFO never meets the rule; (c) when the later batch is **no longer on the stack** (U6's cap, another session's stack, a restart: U6/U18), applying this batch's undo would silently overwrite a change the caller made and can no longer undo; the conservative answer is a conflict (`--partial` skips it, `--drop` drops the step). Judging "own" by pid instead of write identity is mutant (xix). Case class: `own_later_write_off_stack`. |
| S3a | **`already`** (O4's principle: an identical theirs is taken once). A region whose **live facet already equals what the undo would write**, whoever holds it, is **`already`**: it applies nothing and is reported, never a conflict. Value: the live value equals the before-value (for a map key that was absent before, the key is absent). Existence: already deleted (undoing an insert or a restore), or already live (undoing a delete). Position: the element already sits right after S4's anchor. Nothing is overwritten, so there is no ABA hole, and **blame stays with whoever holds it**. Consequences: **(i)** an `already` region is not applied, so it is not pushed for redo (U17): a redo never re-applies someone else's write; **(ii)** in all-or-nothing mode (U13) `already` is not a conflict. Comparing the holder instead of the live state here is mutant (xxvi). Case classes: `own_cell_clear_then_undo`, `already_by_value`. |
| S4 | **Per op** (each the inverse of what the record says the op did): **insert → delete** the key; a conflict unless its position, existence and value holders are own and, for a table row (column), no cell keyed by it is held by a write that **isn't own and isn't in the batch's causal past** (concurrent writes count; this doesn't depend on apply order); if it is already deleted, the region is `already` (S3a). **delete → restore the same key** (undelete): never a conflict; if it is live again (someone restored it), `already` (S3a); a delete concurrent with the undo still wins (engine). **restore → delete**: a conflict unless the existence holder is own **and every undel covering one of the element's deletes that isn't own is in the batch's causal past** (the cell rule's wording above; v1.11 addendum, G1-8 §3's existence holder: when deletes are covered by different undels, the holder is the highest `(lamport, agent)` undel among those covering at least one delete, if every delete is covered). Judging the holder alone lets A's undo of its restore override B's concurrent restore of another delete: mutant (xxvii). *On Yrs (the kit):* a session's history is linear (a second delete of a deleted element writes nothing, a restore of a live one nothing), so an undel not in the batch's causal past came after the batch, is the newest, and holds the facet: the holder test already conflicts; an undel merged from elsewhere has no identity (KC7) and conflicts too. The concurrent case is **model-and-native only**. **move → move back** after the key that was right before it **in place order** before the change, **live or deleted** (a deleted element keeps its place, so it is a valid anchor), or to the start if none was; if that key was dropped, after the nearest kept key before its place, or to the start: a conflict unless the position holder is own, or if the element is deleted. *(v1.11 addendum, agreed by K2 Engine, m_mnjjaNtJfm: was "the nearest live key before that key's place". Anchoring on the deleted key itself puts the element back in its old place among every element, live or deleted, so when the deleted neighbour is restored later the person sees the old order; anchoring on the nearest live key put the element before the neighbour, and its restore reordered the rows: mutant (xxviii). The record's `left` is the element's left neighbours in place order, nearest first, deleted ones included, up to and including the nearest live one (at most 8): a dropped key is skipped (the kit forgets a dropped element's place), so the move goes back after the nearest one still known, or to the start. S3a's position `already` reads the same anchor: right after it in place order.)* **set → set back** (a list value: its value before, `null` included; a map key: its value before, or delete it if it was absent), recording `restores_write` = the facet's holder before the batch (S2): a conflict unless the value holder is own. **map delete → set back** its value before: a conflict unless the holder is own (a later set by anyone conflicts). **drop → nothing**: a dropped element left the live doc for good (native: `drop(elem)` is an absorbing existence state, engine half); a `drop-deleted` batch goes on **no stack** (as `import` and `external`, U4) and its revert conflicts with kind `dropped` (S11). |
| S5 | **Moves of several elements are per element.** A sort, a block move or a reconcile's moves are one batch, one region per moved element (its position). Undo moves back, as **one forward chain** (K-CSV-10b), the moved elements whose position holder is own, left to right in their **pre-change order**, each right after its pre-change left neighbour (the previous one moved back, or S4's anchor). An element someone moved since conflicts (all-or-nothing) or is skipped (`--partial`): never the whole old order restored over a foreign move (mutant (xxiii)). |
| S6 | **Identity is revived, not re-created** (amends U18a for structured kinds). A deleted element comes back by undelete under **its key**, with its value and every cell keyed by it (hidden cells are kept, CSV contract §1.6), where it was. Undo never inserts a new key for an old element (mutants (xxi), (xxii)). By keys, **I1 holds trivially**: one element per key. |
| S7 | **Composite regions** (question 2). A change that writes the table's header setting (`meta.header`: `header on|off`) is **one region**: its names, header quote exceptions, the row it creates or hides, and the setting apply or conflict together, also under `--partial`, because half a header switch reads the file differently from both states. A column rename with the header quote exception it writes is one region too (the name alone already is one facet). Splitting either is mutant (xxiv). |
| S8 | **One step, one change** (E-HIST-6). A step over several roots (a row delete, a sort, a header switch) is one engine change; on Yrs the existing `hist.undo_atomic` deviation applies unchanged to `--steps N`. |
| S9 | **Modes, redo, revert, purge, erasure as written** (U13–U17, U19–U22), "region" read as S1's (S7's). **Identical reports** (U15) per region. **Redo** reapplies exactly the regions the undo applied, each the inverse of what the undo wrote, judged own against the undo's writes (S3): a skipped region is never retried (mutant (iv) carries over). U6's byte bound counts the values a batch's regions hold. |
| S10 | **Revert** (U22) of a structured change uses S1–S8 on its persisted record, "own" meaning **the reverted change's** writes (resolved, S2). It works after a restart (the record and the index are in the store) and inside the revert window. Property (as U22a): on the same state, revert's conflicting regions are a superset of undo's for the same change, and every region both apply gives the same doc. |
| S11 | **Drop is not undo.** `rows drop-deleted` (K-CSV-7, owner only) removes deleted rows and columns and their cells from the live doc; their records keep them, and so does the version it cuts first (`BeforeDrop`, v1.12), whose cell map holds their cells (its lists hold live elements only; restoring an element from it arrives in v0.10.1, and meanwhile the drop's note carries the value to its author). It is on no stack (S4); `revert` of it conflicts (`dropped`); undo or revert of an **earlier** batch that touched a dropped element conflicts with kind `dropped` for that element, **its cells and their quoting included** (v1.12): with `--partial` they are skipped, so nothing is ever written under a dropped key (mutant (xxxi)). |
| S12 | **Restore and dropped keys** (question 3; a history rule, not an undo rule). A version restore (K-HIST-8) is a forward change (U5). A version that holds a key `drop-deleted` removed brings that row back under a **fresh key** (minted), its cells re-keyed: never the old key, because a key is never reused in its causal past (K-CSV-10c; the per-op check of E-SEC-11 refuses it on native). Undo of that restore deletes the fresh keys like any insert. *(Kit v0.10 in progress re-inserts the old key: fixed with this slice, before the engine switch.)* |
| S13 | **A text's re-paired rows** (v1.12; grids only: text undo is untouched). A text (`write --base`, an outside save, `write --base live`) that keeps a row on its key without leaving it exact marks the row at that change; a non-exact column mapping marks the doc instead. A reversal judging change C treats a row of C's record as **rewritten** when its mark is C or later and either a later change holds one of its cell values or its existence (resolved, S2), or a later text marked it (a mark a reversal set isn't a later text). Then no merge by cell: **undo and redo** report each of C's ops on the row as a conflict `rewritten_row`: without `--partial` the whole request conflicts and nothing applies; with `--partial` the row is skipped, reported to the caller as skipped, and the rest applies, so a later redo redoes only what applied; **revert** (U22) puts the row back **whole** to what it held just before C — only a row C kept on its key (marked by C); a row C inserted or deleted isn't marked, keeps S4 per op, and so conflicts if written since — overriding later cells, each with the Overwritten note and a version holding it (if a record left the window or a purge took a value, it can't be known: a conflict). If C remapped the columns and any cell was written since, all of C's ops conflict, for revert too. A reversal step that changes a marked row marks it at its own version, so a client that read the text can't write to it either. Judged on the doc as it stands before the request. A move isn't an edit here. What a reversal emits is one batch of: cell sets, cell deletes (a cell absent just before C; S4 already emits these for a cell set back to absent) and row undels (`ListOp::Restore`). No new op kind and no new batch shape. **S11 before S13 (v1.13):** a row the doc has dropped is `dropped` in every reversal (a revert never rewrites it whole, an undo or redo never calls it `rewritten_row`). |

**Why write identity** (K-HIST-16): a value comparison has an ABA hole. Someone else writes
the same value the batch wrote; v1.9 §6 read "live value = after" and the undo overwrote
their write. By identity their write holds the facet, so it is a conflict (mutant (xv)).

## 7. Reference algorithm

**The kit's implementation:** `session/undo.rs`, used for every engine: `Region::of_change`,
`Region::transform` (edge insertions pulled inside: start `Bias::Before`, end `Bias::After`; a
deletion across an edge taints; the hunks inside the window composed into theirs,
`session/foreign.rs`), `Region::revert` (`merge3_hunks(after, ours, theirs, at_end)`, theirs
read from the live window), `replay_record` (a revert record's edges and theirs from the
stored shapes) and `plan` (newest first, scratch copy, later regions carried).

**What the implementation must have** (each item is a rule above):
1. One region per canonical hunk (U8).
2. One conflict per region in live coordinates, not merge3's sub-conflicts offset by the
   region start (U11).
3. `--partial` (U14), stays-on-top, redo after partial (U17): a partial planner that skips
   conflicting regions, records them on the redo entry, and leaves an all-conflicting step on
   the stack.
4. The end-of-text rule (O5) with `at_end` and a non-empty whole-doc base: `merge3_window`'s
   **caller** folds the whole-doc empty-base flag into `at_end` (the window function itself
   must not test the region's base). Tests: the empty-base conflict and
   `hist.undo_last_line_after_foreign_append`.
5. Bounds (U6): 4 MiB per pid per doc.
6. Purge (U19): a session method that clears every stack for the doc.
7. Revert (U22) and `undo --for` (U2): persisted revert records with carried bounds as
   relative positions or an O(log R) offset tree and lazy taint, the revert window and
   `revert_too_old` (exit 8); the pending on-behalf cap; records kept for pending on-behalf
   changes; purge redacts them.
8. Grouping (U3) and Ctrl+Z with unacked ops (U21): editor clients and the host-side split
   (grouping in kit v0.9.7: `session/live/group.rs`, `undo::compose_group`; U21 later).
   **The oracle has the class since kit v0.9.8:** `spec_undo::model::group`
   (`Model::edit_grouped`: closers (a)–(g) written from U3, agents never group, a joined
   group read off the text as one region, reading R12) and the trace class
   (`tests/trace`, `run_group`: people typing with tokens on the hunk channel, interleaved
   with others' changes inside, touching and away from the group, idle gaps around 500 ms,
   undos and redos; 256 traces in the suite, 10^4 on a node), which catches K4's three
   planted faults (never closes on a foreign change, on idle, on a word boundary).
9. A deterministic diff (D1–D3).
10. The escape from a blocked step (U14): `undo --drop`.
11. Within-step order and shared edges (U8, U10): back-to-front application with carried
    bounds; a shared-edge insertion goes to the left region only.
12. Exact hunk sets (U8, U10, U10a; v1.7): ours as made, theirs carried at element identity;
    no diff of strings anywhere in undo, redo or revert.
13. Provenance (U23, v1.8): a restoration's root stamped by the kit only, path-compressed; an
    index of live restored elements by root (O4a, I1: O(1) per element); windows read by
    root (U8); persisted across restart (store format 5); blame by root (U18a).
14. Structured kinds (§6a, v1.11): batches recorded by key from the applied stream (records
    v3); the holder index (`ELEM_WRITES`, store format 6) with `restores_write` on every
    facet a restoring write holds (S2); own by resolved write identity (S3); a header switch
    as one region (S7); `drop-deleted` on no stack (S11).

## 8. Trace-equivalence test plan (the proof)

| Part | What |
|---|---|
| **Oracle** | `spec_undo::model`: a pure-Rust implementation of U1–U22 and O1–O5 over `String`s and hunks (no engine), written from this document. It **calls the kit's own pipeline, `align_insertions(diff::hunks(..))`** (D1–D2), never a second diff implementation. It is the **oracle of record**, and it implements the `at_end` window flag independently of `merge3_window`'s caller logic. |
| **Generator** | Seeded traces of 2–5 pids × 1–3 connections each × 20–200 steps. Each step is one of: edit (insert, delete or replace at random spots, including end-of-text appends, edge-touching inserts, deletes across others' regions, and **multi-hunk batches** such as a `sed -i` touching distant lines), `undo`, `undo --partial`, `redo`, `redo --partial`, `--steps N`, `revert <change>`, `undo --for`, leave/rejoin, host restart (stacks lost; revert still works), purge (of a random 32-byte secret), and `write --base` including **two writes to an empty doc**; **undo of a last-line delete after a foreign append**; **two regions of one step made to touch by a foreign delete**; **revert outside the window**; `undo --drop`. The alphabet includes multi-byte characters and `\n`. |
| **Run** | Replay each trace through (a) the spec model, (b) the kit sessions on Yrs, (c) the kit sessions on another engine (later). After **every** step compare: the text of every root; the outcome (applied / conflict / partial / stays-on-top / nothing, with its notice); the reported conflict regions (U11) as an exact set; each pid's stack depths; (v1.7) **the applied hunks, exactly** (the same elements on both sides); **U10a on both sides** (the oracle's owners; the kit's per-element blame), by root since v1.8 and over the applied regions since v1.9; and (v1.8) **I1** and **each live character's root author**, on both sides. Every revert also checks U22a's property, and reports U22a's cost: how often revert conflicts on a region where undo of the same change on the same state would apply. **Restart twin** (v1.6): stack-free traces (no undo or redo, which a restart rightly changes) also run on a second kit session that never restarts; after every step its outcome and texts must equal the restarted one's. |
| **Concurrency class** | Later: concurrent client batches integrated between undo steps, with the model consuming the host's applied hunks. It runs on every engine (Yrs integrating client batches in test builds only, behind `untrusted-wire`): **equal wherever the merged texts agree** (generator biased to ≥ 90% agreement) and every other difference **classified by a Def. 4 checker**. It also covers Ctrl+Z with unacked ops (U21) and undo while another client has unacked ops. |
| **Positions** | **Later: not built yet.** A property test on the low-entropy alphabet `{a, \n}` compares each engine's reported hunk positions with a reference model's element positions; a **mutant adapter that derives hunks by diffing text must fail it**. |
| **Volume** | **The target, not run yet** (CI runs 256 traces; `trace_equivalence_large` exists and no script runs it): ≥ 10^5 traces nightly for (a) vs (b), and later for (a) vs (c), with ≥ 10^4 traces per case class (append-at-end, insert inside another's range, multi-hunk partial and stays-on-top, grouping with the (g) split, redo after partial, revert after restart, undo across purge, multi-connection pid, empty-base double write, last-line-delete-after-append, **whole-doc-delete-then-append**, touching regions in one step, revert beyond compaction and outside the window, **revert across restarts with a persisted carry** (v1.6: the window moved past the pending change, then a restart between the change and the revert and between later changes on its root), **repeated text** (an alphabet of `{a, b, \n}`, runs like `aaaa` and identical lines, so that a clean region's merge hunks differ from a re-diff of its window: element identity, U10), **exact sides that differ from a re-diff** (v1.7: F3's class), **concurrent restores of one root** (v1.8: two restorations of one root meet, O4 or O4a decides; and a window element counted as base by root only), **`write --base` over lines that share their first characters** (v0.9.8, `write_base_shared_start`, with the part v0.9.7's character-trimmed sides refused, `write_base_shared_start_was_conflict`), **two different changes of one line, refused** (`write_base_words_same_line`), **a line rewritten into several against the other side's change** (`write_base_multiline_rewrite`), the end of the text's cases A–D (`end_break_a`…`end_break_d`), and the concurrency class; per-kind classes later). **0 mismatches** (concurrency class: as above). Determinism (D3): each trace also runs twice, under load and on aarch64 + x86_64 (**not built yet**, see D3). |
| **D1a classes and mutants** (v1.10) | Case classes, in the oracle, the kit, the conformance suite (`hist.undo_own_only_tokens`) and the traces (`d1_widened`, `d1_widened_then_undone`): **(a)** a line replace over another's recent edit, then the earlier author undoes (their undo conflicts; the replacer's line is untouched); **(b)** two participants change words on adjacent lines, an agent's `write --base` from before merges both, and each undoes their own (v0.9.7.1: the same words in one line are a `write --base` conflict); **(c)** a one-word edit in a long one-line paragraph keeps the co-authors' blame and undo. Mutants: **(xii) `reuse-foreign-elements-in-changed-token`** (no widening) fails (a); **(xiii) `rewrite-whole-line`** (lines as tokens) fails (c); **(xiv) `rewrite-merged-ranges`** (merge3's kept ranges authored too) fails (b). D1a is not yet in the Quint model, so (xii)–(xiv) are kept outside the model check's mutant set until it is. |
| **Model check** | **`MC text-undo` is the kit's**: a Quint model of this spec, replayed against `spec_undo::model` via ITF traces at small bounds (3 pids × 3 events each, plus 2 undos and 1 revert), with a **restart** action (v1.7) so restart transparency is checked inside exhaustive bounds. The engine holds no undo logic, so there is no engine refinement check. Method, abstraction, reductions and results: `docs/MODEL-CHECK.md` (`spec/quint/undo.qnt`, the enumerator `undo_enum`, ITF replay). The 3 × 3 + 2 undos + 1 revert bound is sampled (walks, ITF traces), not exhausted. A transition past the length cap is not checked; a walk records only the violations of the step it picks; U9, U13, U15, U17, U19 and O5 hold by construction on the oracle and the model, so their evidence is their mutants (U13 has none yet); erasure (U9's erased clause) is not modelled, only the trace test reaches it (`docs/MODEL-CHECK.md`, Invariants). |
| **Mutants** | The test must fail on: (i) a whole-text merge3 with no taint rule; (ii) an end-of-text rule without O5; (iii) partial reporting a different set than all-or-nothing; (iv) redo re-trying skipped regions; (v) a diff with a wall-clock deadline (D1), run under a CPU-load harness; **(vi) O5 applied at every window end**; **(vii) O5 conditioned on the region's base instead of the whole doc's**; **(viii) the merge's sides found by re-diffing strings** (v1.7; F3, fails U10a); **(ix) a restart that reads a record region's one taint flag back at both edges** (v1.7; fails restart transparency, U22a); **(x) `provenance-ignored-in-O4`** (v1.8): O4 judged on element identity, so two restorations of one root are never identical, and no O4a: two restorations of one root both land at the doc's end (O5), failing I1; **(xi) `no-o4a`** (v1.9): O4 on (position, root) as specified but no O4a: a root put back beside a foreign insertion at the doc's end (O5 lands both), or in mid-text outside the region's window, is live twice, failing I1. Each mutant is kept with its failing seed, and each has its least counterexample inside an exhaustive bound of the model check. **`write --base`** (v0.9.8; kit-side, `differential::MergeMutant`, caught by the trace classes): v0.9.7's character merge; the final line break always as the live side left it. |
| **Structured kinds** (v1.11) | **Oracle:** `spec_undo::model` gains a **keyed-grid model**: rows and columns as ordered key lists with deleted keys kept in place, cells, names, quoting and meta as maps, every facet with its holder write and `restores_write`; the per-op rules S4–S7 over it, written from §6a. **Generator** (grid traces, 3 pids and an agent on someone's behalf): cell set, clear, block set, row insert, row move, row delete, row restore, column insert, column move, column delete, column restore, rename, header on/off, sort, a block move, write --base on the grid, write --base --partial, an outside save (reconcile), drop-deleted, restart, undo, --steps N, --partial, --drop, redo, revert, undo --for. **Not in the generator:** a version restore (a kit test, a kit-level mutant and K2 Engine's kit diff cover it) and purge (`tests/grid_erasure.rs`). `write --base` is a real run through the kit whose merge comes from the kit's own `merge3_text`: the traces check what follows it, not the merge rule, whose independent checks are the row-pairing property and K2 Engine's model. **(v1.13)** Under `--partial`, a write whose conflicts include a column layout change on either side (any conflict at a column, or a `deleted_col` at a cell or a name) applies **nothing** (ruling (a), the session's `layout_held`): the model applies the merge's clean part only when no such conflict holds it. `tests/grid_traces.rs` fails on a phrase of this list with no step, and on a step no trace reached. **Run:** after every step compare the grid by key (live order, deleted keys, cells, names, meta), the outcome, the conflicting regions as an exact set `(root, key, facet, kind)`, stack depths, each facet's resolved holder, and blame per cell (author, `restored_by`). **Case classes** (≥ 10^4 traces each on a node, 256 in CI): **identical-value write** (ABA: someone else writes the value the batch wrote; S3); **sort vs a foreign move** (S5); **delete, then a foreign cell set in the hidden row, then undo** (the restore brings the cell back with their value; S6); **insert, then a foreign cell set in the new row, then undo** (conflict, S4); **move back past a deleted neighbour** (S4's anchor); **redo after a partial sort undo** (S9); **revert after restart** (S10); **own LIFO chain** (b1 then b2 on one facet, undo, undo: both apply, b2's undo restoring b1's write; S2); **own later write off the stack** (the stack cap or a restart drops b2; undo of b1 conflicts; S3); **write with no identity** (a merged restore or delete; conflicts, KC7: a **pinned Yrs deviation**, S2, not run on native); **own cell clear, then undo, applies** (the clear is a set to `""` or a map delete, and carries the batch's identity: S2); **`already_by_value`** (someone else writes the before-value, then the undo: `already`, nothing applied, not pushed for redo, blame theirs; S3a); **drop between batch and undo** (`dropped`, S11); **`--partial` write over a column change** (v1.13: a `write --base --partial` with a column delete or move on one side beside a cell edit, then undos: nothing applies when a column conflict holds it); **header switch under `--partial`** (one region, S7); **undo across an outside save** (keys kept by the aligner; the save's writes are someone else's); **revert vs undo** (S10's superset property); **move back, then the left neighbour restored** (rows a b c d: someone deletes b; the caller moves c to the start and undoes it; b's delete is undone: c is back after b, and every row's index equals its index before b's delete, relative to the rows live then; v1.11 addendum, S4); **concurrent undels, then undo** (two participants' undels each covering a different concurrent delete, then one undoes its restore: a conflict; v1.11 addendum, S4; **model-and-native only**, its linear form runs on the kit as an IT). **Mutants** that must fail: **(xv) `compare-values`** (§6's "live value ≠ after"; fails ABA); **(xvi) `compare-indices`** (a move judged by its index, not its position holder; a foreign insert elsewhere becomes a false conflict, a foreign move to the same index a missed one); **(xvii) `delete-undone-by-new-key`** (undo of a delete inserts a fresh key; the hidden cells are lost, fails `table.cell_kept`); **(xviii) `redo-retries-skipped`** ((iv) for elements); **(xix) `own-by-pid`** (own judged by author, not write identity; fails `own_later_write_off_stack` by overwriting); **(xx) `restores-not-resolved`** (the holder taken without `restores_write`; fails the own LIFO chain with a false conflict); **(xxi) `undo-restore-by-new-key`** (amendment G1-5 item 15; fails `table.cell_kept`); **(xxii) `drop-revived`** (undo of a batch touching a dropped element re-inserts it; fails S11); **(xxiii) `sort-undo-whole-order`** (undo of a sort restores the whole old order; overwrites a foreign move); **(xxiv) `header-split`** (the header switch per facet under `--partial`; fails S7); **(xxv) `no-identity-is-own`** (a write with no identity counted as own; overwrites, fails KC7); **(xxvi) `already-by-holder`** (`already` judged by the holder instead of the live state; fails `own_cell_clear_then_undo` and `already_by_value`).; **(xxviii) `anchor-on-nearest-live`** (move back after the nearest live key before the old left neighbour, v1.11's first wording; fails `move_back_then_restore_left_neighbour`: the restored neighbour lands after the element); **(xxvii) `own-by-holder-only`** (restore → delete judged by the existence holder alone, not every covering undel; fails `concurrent_undels_then_undo`; **model-and-native only**: on Yrs a linear history makes the two tests agree, S4) |
| **CT names** | `sec.client_provenance_refused` (v1.8), `hist.undo_own_only`, `hist.undo_atomic`, `hist.undo_partial`, `hist.undo_partial_stays_on_top`, `hist.undo_reports_identical`, `hist.redo`, `hist.redo_after_partial`, `hist.undo_eof_append`, `hist.undo_taint`, `hist.undo_purge_clears`, `hist.undo_not_external`, `hist.revert_declined_after_restart`, `hist.revert_too_old`, `hist.revert_over_erased`, `hist.undo_drop_blocked`, `hist.undo_last_line_after_foreign_append`, `hist.undo_touching_regions_one_step`, `merge.empty_base_same_point_conflicts`, `merge.write_base_end_line_break` (O5a; `crates/base/tests/write_base_end.rs`), `hist.undo_group_person` (editor clients only), `hist.ctrl_z_unacked` (editor clients only). **Where each one lives** (a name is a rule's, not always a test's): in `crates/conformance` by that name: `sec.client_provenance_refused`, `hist.undo_own_only`, `hist.undo_atomic`, `hist.undo_partial`, `hist.redo`. In `crates/base/tests/history.rs` as `hist_*` or `merge_*`: `hist_undo_partial_stays_on_top_and_drop` (`undo_partial_stays_on_top`, `undo_drop_blocked`), `hist_undo_partial_and_reports_identical` (`undo_reports_identical`), `hist_redo_after_partial`, `hist_undo_purge_clears`, `hist_revert_declined_after_restart`, `hist_undo_last_line_after_foreign_append`, `merge_empty_base_same_point_conflicts`, `hist_undo_group_person_*`. By another name: `revert_too_old` is `revert_too_old_exit_8_and_window_retention` (history.rs); `revert_over_erased` is `revert_over_purged_text_reports_erased` (erasure.rs). `undo_eof_append` is `f1_each_undoes_their_own_append` (`crates/spec-undo/tests/traces.rs`) and the trace class `append_at_end`. Trace classes and oracle mutants only, **no named session test**: `undo_taint` (class `taint`; mutant (i), `no_taint_fails_u9`; revert's side is `revert_record_taint_on_crossing_delete`), `undo_touching_regions_one_step` (class `touching_regions_one_step`). **Gaps:** `undo_not_external` has no test of its own (`tests/outside_edit_undo.rs` shows an undo after an outside edit reverses the caller's change, not the outside one; none asserts that an import or external change is on no stack); `ctrl_z_unacked` is the concurrency class's, later. |
| **`write --base`** | The same model replays `write --base`, sharing merge3 and O1–O5 (`write --base --partial` is later, `docs/SESSIONS.md` C6: no such verb yet; the model replays it when it lands). **Every engine keeps merge3 for `write --base`** (not a CRDT branch merge), so agents see one semantics on every engine. A CRDT branch merge is a separate, explicit verb. On a grid, `write --base --partial` exists (v0.10.0, §6a): the grid traces replay it (class `partial_write_over_a_column_change`). |
